name: Minanibai-Foia Foia
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only survey/subclassification notes (Usher & Suter 2015); no phonological description of Minanibai-Foia Foia found.

sources.citation: SIL PNG 'PNG Language Resources' pages for mcv and ffi (the Internet Archive 2015) and SIL archive search for ffi (the Internet Archive 2015-09-19).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalogue only: mcv 'Nothing yet available'; ffi lists the 2006 OPD as the sole item.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Inland Gulf'. NewGuineaWorld (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch), DokuWiki raw export.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Proto-Inland Gulf historical phonology only: 'Stress appears to have been contrastive (cf. /*ka'ɸuto/ "smoke" vs. /*gene'ɸo/ "bandicoot") but has not been reconstructed below.' Nothing synchronic on Minanibai-Foia Foia.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2017. The Trans New Guinea family. In B. Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2014. Ethnologue 17th ed., entry Minanibai [mcv] (the Internet Archive 2014-09-25); English Wikipedia 'Minanibai language' (read online 2026-09-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Wikipedia gives unsourced consonant/vowel tables (from the OPD) and no stress remark.

sources.citation: Allen, Karan & Betty Keneqa. 2006. Foia Foia organised phonology data; Foia Foia, Western Province. Ms., 4 pp. SIL PNG (archive item 31013). Bibisa village, after the Emeti Alphabet Development Workshop.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only phonological sketch of the language. p. 3 heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' is left completely blank; 'Syllable Patterns v vc'; no stress marks on any example word or in the sample text. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. Change Request 2006-095 and new code request [ffi] Foia Foia (Phil Carr, SIL PNG, 2007-01-30).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; identification and lexicostatistics (73% with Minanibai); cites only a spelling guide and an unpublished 2006 Emeti workshop report.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid mina1274 Minanibai-Foia Foia; reference records 322531 (Carr 1991 wordlist, 9 pp., unpublished) and 163803 (Johnston 1921, Vocabulary of Eme-Eme, British New Guinea Annual Report 1919-1920: 120).
sources.note: Nothing. 0 descriptive references; Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are wordlists only. Comment: 'Minanibai [mcv] and Foia Foia [ffi] are the same language (Usher and Suter 2015: 16-17)'.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 461-526. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.7.7.5 (p. 511, pdf p. 51), typological notes on Minanibai after Franklin 1973b: consonant and vowel charts, then verbatim 'No information is available on the suprasegmental system.' No stress statement.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1973. Other language groups in the Gulf District and adjacent areas. In K. J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea, 261-277. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 7.42 Minanibai (p. 270) and 7.46 'Comments on Phonology and Grammar' (pp. 272-273): segmental inventory shared by Ipiko/Minanibai/Tao-Suamato, sound correspondences, pronoun table. Nothing on stress or any suprasegmental.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Foia Foia'. NewGuineaWorld, West Inland Gulf (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch), DokuWiki raw export.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phoneme table (12-13 C, 5 V); 'Neither final consonants nor consonant clusters occur.' Correspondence tables reproduce Petterson (2014, Bibisa) and Carr (2006, Pepeha) phonetic forms with stress marks in varying positions ('miɾi, mɑˑ'ɸi, mo'moko, nika'na, 'tebere, ki'ɸɑ, 'inutu ~ i'nut(ˑ)u, sɑ'nia ~ 'sɑniɑ); no synchronic stress rule stated. Also notes 'Minanibai' is not a name speakers recognise.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy & Edgar Suter. 2015. The Anim languages of southern New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 54(1): 110-142.

sources.note: Only refereed modern treatment of Inland Gulf phonology (comparative); pp. 16-17 of the preprint treat Minanibai/Foia Foia and may comment on stress/accent in the family. Closed access; no repository copy found.

sources.citation: Petterson, Robert. 2014. Foeafoea (Foia Foia) of Bibisa village: survey word list, 204 items + 26 phrases, phonetic transcription with stress marks. Unpublished ms., SIL PNG (Ukarumpa).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Fullest phonetic record of the language with stress marked on every item (quoted in NewGuineaWorld); the only primary data from which a stress pattern could be read, and Petterson may have accompanying notes.

sources.citation: Carr, Philip J. 2006. Pepeha (Foia Foia) word list, 164 items + 20 phrases; Carr, Philip J. 1991. Foyafoya (Bibisa) / Minanibai survey word lists, 9 pp. Unpublished mss, SIL PNG (Glottolog ref 322531 for 1991).
